<meta>continues from previous page: ...we will laugh to our hearts' content,</meta>

<term>EV.</term> What birds do I see here? <term>CA.</term> It is the patriarch of the college. Do not withdraw yourself; they have already had their drink; lie down for a little while; once he has departed, we shall converse in our usual manner. <term>EV.</term> Come, I beseech you, tell me what you refused me before. Now that we are alone, tell the whole story, for I would rather learn it from you. <term>CA.</term> Out of so many friends, whom I thought to be of the utmost value, I now realize there was not one who gave me more prudent and mature advice than you, the youngest of all. <term>EV.</term> But in what manner did you overcome the affection of your parents? <term>CA.</term> First, through the wicked exhortations of the monks and nuns; then, my mother’s mind was shaken by my own prayers and blandishments. My father could in no way be compelled. Finally, with all manner of devices brought to bear, he was conquered and overwhelmed, rather than persuaded. It was done over the wine cups; they threatened horrific and wretched ruin if he denied his daughter to Christ. <term>EV.</term> Oh, the wickedness of the foolish! What happened next? <term>CA.</term> I was kept hidden at home for three days; meanwhile, certain women of that college, whom they call <term>Conversas</term> <gloss>converts/lay sisters</gloss>, were always present, adding spirit to my resolve with their exhortations and anxiously taking care that no relative or companion should approach me who might seem capable of changing my mind. In the meantime, the clothes and other things belonging to the feast were being prepared. <term>EV.</term> What was your state of mind meanwhile? Did you waver? <term>CA.</term> No, but I suffered something so horrendous that I would rather die ten times than endure it again. <term>EV.</term> I ask you, what is that? <term>CA.</term> I cannot speak it. <term>EV.</term> What you have said to me, you have said to your friend. <term>CA.</term> Do you promise silence? <term>EV.</term> I would have provided that, even if you had stipulated nothing. As if you did not know me yet.

<summary>Catharina recounts the intense psychological pressure and manipulation by monks and nuns used to force her into religious life, despite her father's initial resistance.</summary>
<keywords>Catharina, Eubulus, monachism, coercion, religious life, manipulation, parental influence</keywords>
